canonical_question: Are the low plasticities (<2%) in the Nb25Mo25Ta25W25 and V20Nb20Mo20Ta20 alloys a result of the vacuum arc-melting process or intrinsic to their chemistry?

question_variants.question: Are the low plasticities (<2%) in the Nb25Mo25Ta25W25 and V20Nb20Mo20Ta20 alloys a result of the vacuum arc-melting process or intrinsic to their chemistry?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The provided text reports low plasticities (<2%) for Nb25Mo25Ta25W25 and V20Nb20Mo20Ta20 alloys produced by vacuum arc-melting. However, the text does not explicitly state whether this low plasticity is intrinsic to the chemistry or a result of the processing method. A comparison with the mechanically alloyed (MA) and spark plasma sintered (SPS) sample in the same paper shows improved plasticity (11.4%), but a direct causal link to the vacuum arc-melting process versus chemistry is not explicitly resolved in the provided evidence spans.

answers.answer: The text reports excellent mechanical properties (11.4% fracture strain) for the NbMoTaWVTi alloy produced by mechanical alloying and SPS. However, it does not explicitly attribute the low plasticity (<2%) observed in vacuum arc-melted alloys (Nb25Mo25Ta25W25 and V20Nb20Mo20Ta20) to a specific cause (process vs. chemistry).
answers.mechanism: Solid solution strengthening, grain boundary strengthening, precipitation strengthening.
answers.boundary_limitation: No direct comparison or causal statement regarding the vacuum arc-melted alloys' low plasticity is provided in the text.
evidence_spans: A NbMoTaWVTi refractory high entropy alloy (HEA) has been successfully synthesized by mechanical alloying (MA) and spark plasma sintering (SPS).
It is observed that only two types of body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solutions are formed in the powders after ball milling for 40 h.
However, a new face-centered cubic (FCC) precipitated phase is observed in the BCC matrix of bulk material consolidated by SPS.
